compare.note.en: Lead with the 2×2. Reach for a specific [archetype](term:archetype) name when it genuinely sharpens the point — or when someone asks.
compare.note.text: 先从 2×2 讲起。只有当特定的[原型](term:archetype)名称确实能让观点更清晰，或有人问起时，再使用它。

compare.options.0.points.0.en: Explaining Org Topologies: the two mandates, the four intelligences and the three topologies.
compare.options.0.points.0.text: 讲解 Org Topologies：两种授权、四种智能和三种拓扑。

compare.options.0.points.1.en: Conversations with leaders about what the organization is designed for — and whether that fits the strategy.
compare.options.0.points.1.text: 与领导者讨论组织为何而设计，以及这是否契合战略。

compare.options.0.points.2.en: Comparing topologies and choosing an org goal.
compare.options.0.points.2.text: 比较各种拓扑，选择组织目标。

compare.options.1.points.0.en: Placing every unit precisely — functional, multi-skill, end-to-end or expanding; tasks up to whole solution.
compare.options.1.points.0.text: 精确安放每个单元：职能型、多技能、端到端或拓展型；从任务直到整体解决方案。

compare.options.1.points.1.en: Seeing small differences that matter, such as a multi-skill team that is still incomplete (CAPS-2) versus an end-to-end one (CAPS-3).
compare.options.1.points.1.text: 看出重要的细微差别，例如仍不完整的多技能团队（CAPS-2）与端到端团队（CAPS-3）。

compare.options.1.points.2.en: Naming the current and target ecosystem in a shared, framework-free language.
compare.options.1.points.2.text: 用一种共享的、不依附于任何框架的语言来命名当前与目标生态系统。

example.ecosystems.0.text.en: Most of the teams are CAPS-2: multi-skilled, yet incomplete, lacking certain capabilities. Functional TASKS-1 specialists support them. That creates dependencies, which CAPS-1 and PART-1 groups manage.
example.ecosystems.0.text.text: 大多数团队是 CAPS-2：多技能，但不完整，缺少某些能力。职能型的 TASKS-1 专家为它们提供支持。这就产生了依赖，由 CAPS-1 和 PART-1 小组来管理。

example.ecosystems.1.text.en: The specialists join the teams, so most teams become CAPS-3: end-to-end, with every skill needed to deliver a whole capability. One team grows into CAPS-4 and learns new skills when the work asks for them. With far fewer dependencies, the CAPS-1 coordination group is no longer needed; a PART-1 group still sets the direction. Together that is a Delivery Topology.
example.ecosystems.1.text.text: 专家加入团队，于是大多数团队成为 CAPS-3：端到端，具备交付一整项能力所需的全部技能。有一个团队成长为 CAPS-4，在工作需要时学习新技能。依赖大幅减少，不再需要 CAPS-1 协调小组；仍由一个 PART-1 小组设定方向。合在一起，就是 Delivery Topology。

lead.en: The 2×2 shows the four intelligences. For detailed mapping of org units there is a [4×4](term:4x4-map) version: four levels on each axis and **16 archetypes** — common patterns of how a unit is structured and operates, each with a short name.
lead.text: 2×2 展示四种智能。要对组织单元做详细的地图绘制，有 [4×4 地图](term:4x4-map)版本：每条轴四个层级，共 **16 个原型**，即单元如何构成和运作的常见模式，每个都有一个简短的名称。

levels.0.items.0.en: **Functional** — specialists in one functional area, e.g. a movie costume department.
levels.0.items.0.text: **职能型**：某一职能领域的专家，例如电影的服装部门。

levels.0.items.1.en: **Multi-skill** — cross-functional but still incomplete, e.g. a surgical team relying on post-op care.
levels.0.items.1.text: **多技能**：跨职能但仍不完整，例如依赖术后护理的外科团队。

levels.0.items.2.en: **End-to-end** — everything needed to deliver complete value, e.g. a software feature team.
levels.0.items.2.text: **端到端**：具备交付完整价值所需的一切，例如软件特性团队。

levels.0.items.3.en: **Expanding** — end-to-end, with the mandate to acquire new skills when needed, e.g. a special-forces team.
levels.0.items.3.text: **拓展型**：端到端，并有权在需要时获取新技能，例如特种部队小队。

levels.1.items.0.en: **Tasks** — fine-grained tasks matching one expertise, e.g. a sous-chef preparing ingredients.
levels.1.items.0.text: **任务**：与某一项专长匹配的细粒度任务，例如备料的副厨师长。

levels.1.items.1.en: **Capabilities** — a full capability (feature, function, service element), e.g. a claims-processing group.
levels.1.items.1.text: **能力**：一整项能力（特性、职能、服务环节），例如理赔处理小组。

levels.1.items.2.en: **Partial solution** — one business vertical, e.g. Uber Ride versus Uber Eats.
levels.1.items.2.text: **部分解决方案**：一个业务垂直领域，例如 Uber Ride 与 Uber Eats。

levels.1.items.3.en: **Whole solution** — holistic problems and customer value, with no permanent separation inside the unit, e.g. a two-person Instagram-like startup.
levels.1.items.3.text: **整体解决方案**：整体性的问题和客户价值，单元内部没有永久的分隔，例如类似 Instagram 的两人创业公司。

naming.text.en: The **prefix** names the work-mandate row (TASKS, CAPS, PART, WHOLE); the **digit** names the skills-mandate column, counting from the left. So CAPS-3 reads “end-to-end @ capability” — a complete unit, output-oriented, in the Delivering group.
naming.text.text: **前缀**表示工作授权所在的行（TASKS、CAPS、PART、WHOLE）；**数字**表示技能授权所在的列，从左数起。因此 CAPS-3 读作“端到端 @ 能力”：一个完整单元，面向产出，属于 Delivering 一组。

note.text.en: A simple notation and a few sentences describe a whole ecosystem, so it can be grasped as a whole, its challenges recognized, and a conversation about improving it can begin. Not team by team: improvements at the team level rarely stick. The units of an ecosystem depend on each other, so they have to be improved together, as one system.
note.text.text: 一套简单的记法和几句话，就能描述整个生态系统，让人从整体上把握它、认清它的挑战，并展开如何改进的对话。不是逐个团队地做：团队层面的改进很少能持久。生态系统中的各个单元相互依赖，所以必须作为一个系统一起改进。
